tools.name: source_status
tools.description: Use this tool when the user asks whether the OpenNIH corpus is loaded, which official sidecars are available, or how stale the data might be — and before reporting 'no such grant', since corpus_lag_note explains that a grant added to RePORTER after the snapshot cutoff is absent here, not nonexistent

tools.name: search_grants
tools.description: Use this tool when the user asks to find NIH grants — by topic, principal investigator, institution, NIH Institute/Center, activity code, fiscal year, or project number ('what NIH grants exist on CRISPR', 'show me Stanford's R01s in 2022', 'look up 5R01CA036569-02'). This is the primary entry point:

tools.name: rank_institutions
tools.description: Use this tool when the user asks which institutions get the most NIH money — 'top NIH-funded universities', 'where does NCI money go', 'rank research hospitals by R01 funding'. It also yields the entity_id that get_institution_profile, mechanism_mix and funding_growth take. Ranks institutions by com

tools.name: get_pi_profile
tools.description: Use this tool when the user asks about one researcher — 'how much NIH funding does Dr. X have', 'list this PI's grants', 'who does she collaborate with'. Run search_grants (or the find-pi-funding prompt) first: profile_id is the NIH RePORTER PI identifier carried in each result's pi_profile_id field

tools.name: get_institution_profile
tools.description: Use this tool when the user asks about one named institution — 'what is Harvard's NIH funding history', 'which PIs does this university fund', 'what mechanisms does it win'. Call rank_institutions first to obtain the entity_id; search_grants results do NOT carry one. Read-only institution profile: f

tools.description: Use this tool to get yearly NIH funding totals and grant counts. Returns a time series for the whole NIH, one Institute/Center, one activity code, or one institution. tools.name: search
tools.description: Use this tool when a Deep Research or connector client needs citation-shaped NIH grant hits for a natural-language query. Returns {"results": [{id, title, text, url}]} where id is the NIH project_num to pass to fetch and url is the public OpenNIH grant page. Each record is PROJECT-level, not project

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Use this tool to retrieve the full record for one NIH grant after search returned its id. Returns {id, title, text, url, metadata} with url set to the public OpenNIH grant page so the client can cite it. This is the OpenAI Deep Research compatibility wrapper around the same canonical-row resolver se

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_institution_profile" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: source_status, get_pi_profile, search, fetch · Private data: search_grants, search, fetch · Public sink: activity_code_distribution, institution_concentration · Destructive: get_pi_profile.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: source_status, get_pi_profile, search, fetch · Private data: search_grants, search, fetch · Public sink: activity_code_distribution, institution_concentration · Destructive: get_pi_profile

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
